Beskrivning
Originally published in 1897, this two-volume work chronicles the polar expedition of Norwegian scientist Fridtjof Nansen (1861-1930), who came closer than any previous explorer to the North Pole. Beginning on board his boat, the Fram, which was deliberately driven into pack-ice off Siberia in order to drift north, Nansen and his companions later resorted to sleds and kayaks. Volume 2 describes the journey over the ice - setting out with 28 dogs, 3 sledges and 2 kayaks - and ends with an account of the return journey. Quick Summary

The "Farthest North" refers to the title of a book by Norwegian explorer Fridtjof Nansen, detailing his 1893 expedition aboard the ship Fram . Nansen's daring plan was to freeze the Fram into Arctic ice off Siberia and allow the currents to carry it across the Arctic Ocean towards Spitsbergen. This expedition aimed to scientifically investigate the Arctic Ocean and potentially reach the North Pole. 1 2
Nansen and his companion, Hjalmar Johansen, left the Fram in 1895 to attempt a sledge journey to the pole, reaching a record latitude of 86°14′ N before turning back. The Fram itself safely completed its drift, releasing from the ice north of Spitsbergen in 1896, having collected significant scientific data. Nansen's book, Farthest North , published in 1897, documented this remarkable journey. 2 1
